title.en: Presales department: which team structure works?
title.ja: プリセールス部：どのチーム編成がうまくいくか

summary.en: A presales department for server hardware. Deals arrive from sales, engineers size and quote them, customers decide. Try four team structures and see what happens to speed, wins and people.
summary.ja: サーバー用 PC のプリセールス部。営業から案件が来て、エンジニアが構成と見積もりを作り、お客さまが決める。4 つのチーム編成を試して、速さ・受注・人への影響を見る。

scenario.en: Simulate a presales department that supports sales of server hardware (general servers, GPU / AI servers, storage, network). Deals arrive every day with different sizes, difficulty and deadlines. Compare team structures: one shared pool, product squads, account pods, and a triage desk with specialists. Which one answers fastest, wins most, and burns people out least?
scenario.ja: サーバー用 PC（汎用サーバー、GPU・AI サーバー、ストレージ、ネットワーク）の営業を支えるプリセールス部をシミュレートしてほしい。案件は毎日届き、金額も難しさも締め切りも違う。チーム編成を比べたい。共有プール、製品別の班、顧客別の担当、一次受付と専門チーム。どれが一番速く答え、一番受注し、人を疲れさせないか。

questions.en: Which team structure wins the most revenue over six months?
questions.ja: 半年で一番受注できるチーム編成はどれか。

questions.en: Where do deals wait: for a specialist, for a handoff, or for an approval?
questions.ja: 案件はどこで待たされるか。専門家か、引き継ぎか、承認か。

questions.en: What breaks first when GPU demand doubles?
questions.ja: GPU の需要が 2 倍になったとき、最初に壊れるのはどこか。

assumptions.en: Every number is an assumption: deal mix, work hours per stage, skill effects, win rates.
assumptions.ja: 案件の構成、工程ごとの作業時間、スキルの効果、受注率は、すべて仮定の値。

assumptions.en: The same deals arrive in every branch of a run, so structures can be compared fairly.
assumptions.ja: 分岐しても届く案件は同じにしてあるので、編成を公平に比べられる。

assumptions.en: Quality depends on the skill of whoever did the work; lateness lowers the chance of winning; public tenders are lost if late.
assumptions.ja: 品質は作業した人のスキルで決まる。遅れると受注率が下がる。官公庁の入札は、遅れたら失注とする。

name.ja: プリセールスのマネージャー

agents.persona: The presales manager, a former engineer. Measured on win rate and on how fast sales gets answers. Tries to protect the team from overload but gives in when a big customer or a senior sales director pushes.

The head of the department. Owns a limited budget and reports quarterly revenue upward. Prefers changes that show results within a quarter, is sceptical of reorganisations, and worries about losing experienced people.

Senior presales engineers, 10+ years. Everyone asks them for help. Proud of accurate designs and unwilling to send out sloppy quotes. They quietly take on overtime, then burn out and get calls from recruiters.
Mid-level presales engineers. Solid on their own product area, slower outside it. They want to grow and to go home on time; they push back on unrealistic deadlines more openly than seniors.
Junior presales engineers, 1-3 years. Eager, afraid of making sizing mistakes, slow without templates. They rarely refuse work and are tempted to copy an old configuration to save time.

Sales reps with quarterly quotas. Every one believes their own deal is the urgent one. They escalate when answers are slow, and some send their own rough quote rather than wait. Small deals are not worth a long queue to them.

IT buyers at enterprises, public bodies, small firms and AI startups comparing two or three vendors. They expect an answer by the promised date; a late answer signals a vendor that will also be late with delivery. Startups move fastest.
